diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $\delta\in (0, \frac{1}{m}]$, we define the regularized feasible set $\mathcal P_{m}(\delta)\\coloneq \left\{\bm q\in\R^m: \|\bm q\|_1 = 1, \bm q\geq \delta\right\}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Moving $\bm q_n^*$ along $\bm a$ keeps the objective unchanged only if $\sum_i \frac{a_i}{\sigma_i^2(x_i)}R_iR_i^\top = 0$ (so $\bm U$, hence $H$, is unchanged), but it keeps the iterate feasible in $\mathcal P_m(\delta)$ only if also $\sum_i a_i = 0$ (to preserve $\|\bm q\|_1 = 1$). The stated linear dependence provides no control of $\sum_i a_i$, so the perturbed point generically leaves the simplex and is not a feasible optimizer. Moreover, at the critical size $|\supp_\delta| = n(n+1)/2+1$ the dependence space of $\{R_iR_i^\top\}_{i\in\supp_\delta}$ in $\mathrm{Sym}_n$ is one-dimensional and may contain no direction with $\sum_i a_i = 0$; the argument as written yields at best the weaker bound $n(n+1)/2+1$. The sharp bound follows instead from the KKT sensitivity equality ($\tr(\bm U^{-1}R_iR_i^\top\bm U^{-1})$ is constant on $\supp_\delta$) plus a Carathéodory/vertex argument, or from the reduction $q_i = \delta + r_i$ to classical A-optimal design, whose support is at most $n(n+1)/2$. The claim itself is true; the proof is defective.

failure_location.quote: Note that if $|\supp_{\delta}(\bm q_n^{*})|>n(n+1)/2$, the corresponding $R_iR^\top_i, i\in\text{supp}_{\delta}(\bm q^{*}_n)$ are linearly dependent. Therefore, there exists a direction $\bm a = (a_1, \ldots, a_m)^\top$ supported on $\text{supp}_{\delta}(\bm q^{*}_n)$ such that  $\sum_{i\in [m]}\frac{a_i}{\sigma^2(x_i)}R_iR^\top_i = 0$. Applying a perturbation argument for $\bm q^{*}_n$ along $\bm a$ yields another optimal solution that has a smaller $\delta$-support.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the perturbation argument by the standard support-size argument for A-optimal designs: writing $q_i = \delta + r_i$ turns the problem into minimizing $\tr((\bm U_\delta + Lm\sum_i r_i \sigma_i^{-2} w_i^{-1} R_iR_i^\top)^{-1})$ over the simplex, a classical A-optimality problem admitting an optimal solution with support at most $n(n+1)/2$ (Pukelsheim's support theorem); equivalently, derive the KKT sensitivity equality and apply Carathéodory's theorem in the affine hyperplane $\{\bm M \in \mathrm{Sym}_n : \tr(\bm U^{-2}\bm M) = \mathrm{const}\}$.
issues.overall_effect: The sparsity statement $|\supp_\delta(\bm q_n^*)| \le n(n+1)/2$ is unproven as written. No downstream result uses the sparsity bound (only the convexity and existence of $\bm q_n^*$, which are correctly proved), so Theorems thm:main and thm:conv are unaffected.
issues.title: Lemma lmjh: proof of the sparsity bound uses a perturbation that need not stay feasible
issues.why_classification: The claimed bound is true and standard; a routine citation or a short optimality-conditions argument repairs the proof with no loss of content and no downstream impact.

(Reweighted least-squares) Compute $\bm p_n$ as an optimal solution $\bm q^{*}_n$ to \eqref{H-conv+}.

issues.failure_explanation: The reweighted branch computes $\bm q_n^*$ by minimizing $H$ over $\mathcal P_m(\delta)$. This feasible set is empty whenever $\delta > 1/m$ (since $\|\bm q\|_1 = 1$ together with $\bm q \ge \delta$ forces $1 \ge m\delta$), so for such inputs the allocation step is infeasible and the algorithm is not well defined. The theory (Lemma mkjh, Lemma lm:a2) is stated for $\delta \in (0, 1/m]$, but the algorithm's input list specifies only $\delta > 0$.
issues.overall_effect: Only the input-output contract of Algorithm alg:1 in the reweighted branch; all theoretical results already assume $\delta \in (0, 1/m]$, and the numerics use $\delta = 0.01/m$.
issues.title: Algorithm alg:1: the input specification for delta omits the upper bound delta <= 1/m, making the reweighted branch infeasible
issues.why_classification: A one-line input-specification fix restores well-definedness; no mathematical content is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Gauss-Markov gives $H(\bm p) = \tr\Cov[\widehat{\bm\alpha}_{wm}] \le \tr\Cov[\widehat{\bm\alpha}_{unw}] = \E\|\widehat{\bm\alpha}_{unw} - \bar{\bm\alpha}\|^2$, and the last quantity is bounded by $\|(\bm V^\top\bm W\bm V)^{-1}\|_2^2\,G(\bm p)$ (see the proof of Lemma lm:a1). The remark drops the factor $\|(\bm V^\top\bm W\bm V)^{-1}\|_2^2$, which exceeds $1$ in general: on the event $\AA$ the singular values of $\bm W^{1/2}\bm V$ may lie in $[0.9, 1)$, giving $\|(\bm V^\top\bm W\bm V)^{-1}\|_2 > 1$ (up to $(0.9)^{-2}$), and off $\AA$ it is unbounded. Hence neither the pointwise inequality $H(\bm p_n^*) \le G(\bm p_n^*)$ nor the resulting unconditional comparison $\E_\XX[H(\bm q_n^*)] \le \E_\XX[G(\bm p_n^*)]$ is established; the best available statement is $H(\bm q_n^*) \le (0.9)^{-4}G(\bm p_n^*)$ on $\AA$.

failure_location.quote: By setting $\delta \leq \frac{1}{m\sqrt{J_n}}$, it can be verified using \eqref{neyman} that $\bm p_n^*\in\mathcal P_m(\delta)$ so that $H(\bm q^{*}_n)\\leq H(\bm p_n^*)\leq G(\bm p_n^*)$ (the first inequality follows from the definition of $\bm q_n^*$ and the second uses the Gauss--Markov theorem), which implies $\E_\XX[H(\bm q^{*}_n)]\leq \E_\XX[G(\bm p_n^*)]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the comparison on the event $\AA$ with the condition-number factor, i.e., $H(\bm q_n^*) \le \|(\bm V^\top\bm W\bm V)^{-1}\|_2^2 G(\bm p_n^*) \le (0.9)^{-4}G(\bm p_n^*)$ on $\AA$, and draw the qualitative conclusion from that.
issues.overall_effect: Only the informal variance comparison in Remark rem:compare between the reweighted and non-reweighted allocations; the main theorems do not use this inequality.
issues.title: Remark rem:compare: the comparison H(q_n*) <= G(p_n*) is unjustified and fails in general
issues.why_classification: The remark is explicitly qualitative; inserting the absolute constant factor valid on $\AA$ preserves the comparison's point, so the repair is local and no guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The boosting uses $l = \lfloor n/k \rfloor$ independent blocks, each succeeding with probability at least $1/2$, giving success probability at least $1 - 2^{-l}$, which requires $l \ge \log_2(1/\delta)$. The hypothesis $n > 1.5\log(1/\delta)k$ only yields $l \ge \lfloor 1.5\log(1/\delta)\rfloor$, and the inequality $2/\log 2 < 3$ (i.e., $\log_2(1/\delta) < 1.5\log(1/\delta)$) ignores the integrality of $l$. Whenever $\lfloor 1.5\log(1/\delta)\rfloor < \log_2(1/\delta)$ — e.g., $\delta = e^{-3}$, where $\log_2(1/\delta) \approx 4.33$ but $\lfloor 1.5\log(1/\delta)\rfloor = 4$ — parameters satisfying the hypothesis (e.g., $n = 4.6k$) give only $1 - 2^{-4} = 0.9375 < 1 - \delta = 0.9502$, so the stated conclusion is not established by the argument.

failure_location.quote: Choosing $l\geq \log(1/\delta)/\log 2$ and noting $2/\log 2<3$ yields the desired result.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to $n \ge k\lceil\log_2(1/\delta)\rceil$ (equivalently $n > k(\log_2(1/\delta)+1)$); the sample complexity remains $\Theta(k\log(1/\delta))$, so the result's character is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The baseline approximation-capacity result of Theorem thm:rb is unproven for a range of $(\delta, n)$ with $\lfloor n/k\rfloor < \log_2(1/\delta)$; it is cited only qualitatively in the introduction and the numerical section, and no formal result depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds $\min_{v\in V_n}\|f-v\|$ by constructing $f_n = g_n - \sum_{i\in[s]}\theta_i h_i$ with $h_i = g_{2i} - g_{2i-1}$, which involves all $2s$ basis functions (generically $\|f_n\|_0 = 2s$), not at most $k$. Hence $f_n \in V_n$ but $f_n \notin \bar V_{n,k}$ unless $2s \le k$. The proof sets $n = 2s$ with $s = c'r(\log r)^3$ while the theorem allows $k = \lceil C_1 r(\log r)^3\rceil$ with $C_1$ independent of $c'$, so the required compatibility $k \ge 2s$ (i.e., $C_1 \ge 2c'$) is neither stated nor argued, and the closing boosting sentence does not address support size at all. Consequently the inequality $\min_{v\in\bar V_{n,k}}\|f-v\| \le 24\sqrt{r\tau_{r+1}}$ — the substance of the theorem — is unproven; the proof establishes only the weaker full-space bound $\min_{v\in V_n}\|f-v\| \le 24\sqrt{r\tau_{r+1}}$ with constant probability.
